rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a nanoscale Al2O3 interlayer between Cr and Zr-alloy, while the target paper uses compositionally varied AlTiCrZrNbTa refractory high-entropy alloy coatings. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions (a diffusion-barrier interlayer vs. a compositionally tuned coating), so the specific lever is entirely different.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis mentions subcritical water (300–400°C) and high-temperature steam (900–1000°C), while the target paper uses isothermal oxidation in flowing steam at 1000°C and 1100°C. Both involve high-temperature steam oxidation, which is the same broad regime, but the hypothesis lacks the paper's specific temperatures (1000°C, 1100°C), exposure times (60 min, 30 min), steam flow rate, and post-oxidation indentation conditions.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes a physical diffusion barrier that limits Cr–Zr interdiffusion. The target paper's mechanism involves formation of a dense Al2O3-TiO2-Cr2O3 composite oxide layer that suppresses oxygen diffusion and preserves adhesion, with excess Al causing intermetallic formation and oxide discontinuity. These are different general classes of mechanism (diffusion barrier vs. protective oxide formation).
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts reduced interdiffusion and improved adhesion/performance relative to unmodified Cr coating. The target paper predicts and measures a minimum oxidation rate and oxygen penetration at an intermediate Al content (~10 at.%) with reversal at higher Al. Both involve improved protective performance, but the predicted property (interdiffusion vs. oxidation rate/oxygen penetration) and the specific comparison (Al2O3 interlayer vs. unmodified Cr vs. Al content optimization) differ.
